heading: Chap. vii.—Avoid the Docetæ, and persevere in fasting and prayer.
paragraphs:
“For whosoever does not confess that Jesus Christ has
come in the flesh, is antichrist;”[356] and whosoever does not
confess the testimony of the cross,[357] is of the devil; and whosoever
perverts the oracles of the Lord to his own lusts, and
says that there is neither a resurrection nor a judgment, he
is the first-born of Satan. Wherefore, forsaking the vanity
of many, and their false doctrines, let us return to the word
which has been handed down to us from[358] the beginning;
“watching unto prayer,”[359] and persevering in fasting; beseeching
in our supplications the all-seeing God “not to lead
us into temptation,”[360] as the Lord has said: “The spirit truly
is willing, but the flesh is weak.”[361]
